James Okafor 95 once spent a weekend debugging a firmware glitch that caused a critical ad server to crash during a live campaign. He arrived at the office before dawn, methodically tracing the issue through layers of C code and RTOS scheduling. By morning, he’d rewritten a memory management routine, restoring stability and saving the team from a potential $20k loss. This incident revealed his knack for marrying technical precision with relentless problem-solving—qualities that define his work at AdVerve.  

As an embedded engineer, James thrives at the intersection of hardware and software. He’s built firmware for edge devices that process real-time ad data, ensuring low-latency communication via MQTT protocols. His ability to align sensor hardware with software pipelines has streamlined AdVerve’s IoT integrations, reducing debugging cycles by 30%. Colleagues often remark on his calm under pressure, whether troubleshooting a failing prototype or refactoring legacy code for scalability.  

Beyond technical skill, James brings a rare curiosity. He’s self-taught in RTOS optimization, applying this knowledge to balance performance and power constraints in adtech hardware. His collaborative spirit and attention to detail make him a trusted peer, though he’s never satisfied with “good enough”—he insists on refining solutions until they’re robust.  

James is ready to take on challenges that demand both depth of expertise and adaptability. His work ethic and technical acumen make him a standout candidate for roles requiring precision and innovation. I’d welcome the chance to discuss how he might contribute to your team.
